title: Duplicate queue/claimer: core/portfolio.py enqueue/claim/finish duplicates core/job_manager.py on the same jobs DB; backlog.accept(when='now') bypasses run_entry
body: Found in PFSSOT-P0 reuse map. Two claimers on data/portfolio/portfolio.db violate the 'one queue' rule (doc section 41) and create a submission bypass. Must converge on job_manager before adding worker leases.

rcca.root_cause: core/portfolio.py retains a legacy enqueue/claim/finish operating on the SAME jobs table as core/job_manager.py (data/portfolio/portfolio.db). Two claimers exist for one queue: job_manager.claim (canonical) and portfolio.claim (legacy), and backlog.accept(when='now') calls portfolio.enqueue, bypassing the canonical run_entry -> job_manager path.
five_why: 1. Why two claimers? job_manager was added as the canonical queue, but portfolio's older queue code was never retired.
2. Why is that a defect? It is a second scheduler/queue over one store (doc section 41 forbids it) and a submission bypass.
3. Why does backlog.accept use it? accept() predates run_entry and still calls portfolio.enqueue directly.
4. Why not caught? No gate asserts a single claim/submission path across core/.
5. Why does it matter now? The scheduler/worker extension must converge on ONE claimer or behavior diverges.
rcca.corrective: Make portfolio.enqueue/claim/finish delegate to core.job_manager (single writer); route backlog.accept(when='now') through core.run_entry.enqueue; keep portfolio as a thin compatibility layer, not a second claimer.
rcca.preventive: Add a gate asserting one claimer (only job_manager does BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim) and one submission path (run_entry.enqueue) in core/.
